propositions.text: Rose-Marie Sahadeo seeks judicial review of a Federal Public Sector Labour Relations and Employment Board decision.
The Board decision addressed grievances about disciplinary measures and termination during OIDP training to become a CBSA officer.
The Board also addressed grievances alleging discrimination, breach of management-rights clause, and disguised discipline.

paragraphs.summary: The court states that Ms. Sahadeo seeks judicial review of a Board decision addressing her disciplinary and discrimination grievances during OIDP training.

propositions.text: The Board allowed grievances on disciplinary measures and termination, reducing or setting aside suspensions and termination.
The Board awarded Ms. Sahadeo three months salary and benefits reflecting remaining OIDP training time.
The Board determined Ms. Sahadeo should be reinstated at the beginning of the OIDP.

paragraphs.summary: The Board allowed some grievances, awarded three months salary and benefits, and reinstated Ms. Sahadeo at OIDP start.

propositions.text: Ms. Sahadeo argues she should have full retroactive salary and benefits, not just three months.
She argues she should be reinstated at her training stage reached, not at the beginning.
She argues the Board erred in denying her discrimination grievance.

paragraphs.summary: Ms. Sahadeo argues for full retroactive pay, reinstatement at her training stage, and that discrimination grievance denial was erroneous.

propositions.text: The parties agree the standard of review is reasonableness.
The court concurs that reasonableness is the applicable standard.

paragraphs.summary: The court and parties agree the standard of review is reasonableness.

propositions.text: Vavilov decision guides reasonableness review focusing on decision and reasoning process.
Reasonableness requires justification, transparency, intelligibility, and defensible outcomes.
Reviewing court should not substitute its own reasons for flawed administrative decisions.
A decision is unreasonable if reasons fail to show rational analysis or are unclear on critical points.
Consistency with past decisions is a constraint; departures require explanation or decision is unreasonable.
Harsh consequences require reasons reflecting the stakes and legislative intent.

paragraphs.summary: The court cites Vavilov for reasonableness review principles including justification, transparency, and need for clear reasons.

propositions.text: Ms. Sahadeo was reinstated because the Board found her termination for unsatisfactory performance unreasonable.
This aspect of the Decision is not in issue.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes reinstatement due to unreasonable termination is not contested.

propositions.text: The Board awarded only three months pay and benefits, reflecting remaining training time.
The Board recognized it could not promote Ms. Sahadeo and that completion of training was not guaranteed.

paragraphs.summary: The Board limited pay to three months and recognized it could not promote Ms. Sahadeo or guarantee training success.

propositions.text: Usual practice is reinstatement with compensation from dismissal date to reinstatement date.
This applies to probationary employees as well.
Training status is not a basis to deny full retroactive pay and benefits.
Reasonableness requires explanation if tribunal departs from normal practice.

paragraphs.summary: Ms. Sahadeo argues usual practice is full retroactive pay including probationary employees, requiring explanation if departed from.

propositions.text: The Board could reasonably award three months pay; remedy decisions deserve deference.
Bahniuk describes full back pay as common but not default outcome.
Bahniuk involved compensation in lieu of reinstatement, not full back pay.

paragraphs.summary: The Crown argues the Board's three-month pay award was reasonable and Bahniuk does not mandate full back pay.

propositions.text: Bahniuk is distinguishable as it was forward-looking, unlike this rearward-looking case.
Bergey mentions this forward/rearward distinction.

paragraphs.summary: Ms. Sahadeo replies Bahniuk is distinguishable because it was forward-looking, unlike this case.

propositions.text: The Board had broad power to craft remedy and court should not lightly interfere.
Facts here may differ from Bahniuk which involved dismissal for cause, not unsatisfactory performance.

paragraphs.summary: The court agrees the Board had broad remedial power and notes factual differences from Bahniuk.

propositions.text: The Board failed to adequately explain limiting pay and benefits to three months versus eight years.
Board's reasoning on this is brief and found in paragraphs 448-449 of the Decision.
Paragraph 448 orders three months pay to make Ms. Sahadeo whole.
Paragraph 449 limits jurisdiction to reinstating Ms. Sahadeo to OIDP start and notes two unreasonable assessment periods.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Board inadequately explained limiting pay to three months and quotes relevant Decision paragraphs.

propositions.text: The Board tied back pay to remaining training time and recognized it could not award promotion.
The Board did not explain why back pay was limited to three months.
Possibility of unsuccessful training may have influenced Board but was not stated.
Board viewed three months pay as making Ms. Sahadeo whole, but this is unjustified.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Board tied pay to training time but failed to explain limiting pay and unjustifiably viewed three months as making whole.

propositions.text: The Board's limitation of compensation award was unreasonable given its conclusion of improper termination.

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes the Board's limitation of compensation was unreasonable.

propositions.text: The Board was not obliged to award full back pay retroactive to termination date.
The Board's failure was inadequate explanation for not awarding full back pay.
The issue is remitted to the Board for reconsideration.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Board could limit pay but must explain; remits issue for reconsideration.

propositions.text: The Board ruled Ms. Sahadeo should be reinstated at the beginning of OIDP.
Ms. Sahadeo argues she should be reinstated at her training stage reached, three months from end.

paragraphs.summary: The Board reinstated Ms. Sahadeo at OIDP start; she argues for reinstatement at her training stage.

propositions.text: Ms. Sahadeo recently completed OIDP and is now a BSO.
Ms. Sahadeo acknowledges reinstatement stage issue is almost moot now.
The issue is relevant to her service clock with financial implications and not moot.

paragraphs.summary: Ms. Sahadeo completed OIDP; she acknowledges reinstatement stage issue is almost moot but relevant to service clock.

propositions.text: The question is whether the Board's reinstatement at OIDP start was reasonable.

paragraphs.summary: The court frames the issue as whether reinstatement at OIDP start was reasonable.

propositions.text: The Board has expertise in reinstatement after unjust dismissal.
The Board could not promote Ms. Sahadeo, only reinstate to OIDP.
Ms. Sahadeo was absent almost eight years from termination to Decision.
Her success in training was uncertain.
The Board concluded reinstatement at OIDP start was the only way to make her whole.
Restarting OIDP balances fairness with operational realities and public confidence.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes Board expertise, inability to promote, long absence, uncertain success, and fairness balancing operational needs.

propositions.text: Ms. Sahadeo argues the Board did not consider the long period without training or work as BSO.
Vavilov instructs courts not to add reasons to support administrative decisions.

paragraphs.summary: Ms. Sahadeo argues Board ignored long absence; court notes Vavilov forbids adding reasons to support decisions.

propositions.text: Board's finding at paragraph 449 that Ms. Sahadeo would be made whole by restarting training is not entirely clear
Board acknowledged its jurisdiction is limited to reinstating Ms. Sahadeo to the OIDP
Board had to decide at what stage of OIDP Ms. Sahadeo should be reinstated

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Board's unclear finding about restarting Ms. Sahadeo's training and notes the Board's limited jurisdiction and decision on reinstatement stage.

propositions.text: Board was concerned about Ms. Sahadeo's ability to complete training successfully and saw restarting as best remedy
Board was aware of long time since termination and effect on training value
Court understands Board's analysis as reasonable under Vavilov despite not being explicit

paragraphs.summary: The court infers the Board's concern about training success and time lapse, finding the analysis reasonable under Vavilov.

propositions.text: Board addressed discrimination grievance at paragraphs 458-487 and denied it

paragraphs.summary: The court states the Board denied the discrimination grievance in paragraphs 458-487.

propositions.text: Discrimination grievance based on 'No Discrimination' clause prohibiting gender and colour discrimination
Ms. Sahadeo is a black woman
Ms. Sahadeo cited belittling remarks, refusal to remove false sick leave allegation, unequal discipline, atypical termination announcement, and differential treatment

paragraphs.summary: The court summarizes Ms. Sahadeo's discrimination grievance based on protected characteristics and various alleged discriminatory acts.

propositions.text: Board applied correct legal test requiring prima facie case with three elements
Board recognized no need to prove intent and must examine all circumstances including circumstantial evidence
Board noted mere suspicions of discrimination are insufficient

paragraphs.summary: Ms. Sahadeo acknowledges the Board applied the correct legal test for discrimination and recognized circumstantial evidence importance.

propositions.text: Board accepted Ms. Sahadeo met first two prima facie requirements but failed third
Board considered each allegation and found none established prima facie discrimination

paragraphs.summary: The Board found Ms. Sahadeo met first two discrimination elements but failed the third, rejecting all allegations as prima facie discrimination.

propositions.text: Ms. Sahadeo argues Board improperly excluded unequal discipline from discrimination assessment
Board found grievance on 15-day suspension did not allege CHRA breach and excluded it from discrimination grievance

paragraphs.summary: Ms. Sahadeo argues exclusion of unequal discipline was improper; Board excluded it as grievance did not allege discrimination then.

propositions.text: Ms. Sahadeo argues discrimination was implicit in unequal discipline complaint and cites Parry Sound for form over substance

paragraphs.summary: Ms. Sahadeo contends discrimination was implicit in unequal discipline complaint and Board erred excluding it, citing Parry Sound.

propositions.text: Court finds Board reasonably inferred discrimination was not contemplated in suspension grievance
Board's finding does not conflict with Supreme Court guidance in Vavilov

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Board reasonably inferred no discrimination claim in suspension grievance and did not err under Vavilov.

propositions.text: Ms. Sahadeo argues unequal discipline circumstances merited close Board examination
Board did consider those circumstances and reached a conclusion
Court cannot find Board's analysis unreasonable by substituting its own conclusion

paragraphs.summary: Ms. Sahadeo argues for close examination of unequal discipline; court finds Board did so and court cannot substitute its own conclusion.

propositions.text: Ms. Sahadeo argues Board failed to consider incidents as a whole as required

paragraphs.summary: Ms. Sahadeo argues the Board failed to consider all incidents together as required.

propositions.text: Court disagrees and cites Board's explicit citation of Turner for considering all circumstantial evidence
Turner requires considering all circumstantial evidence and nexus to prohibited ground for discrimination

paragraphs.summary: The court disagrees and notes the Board cited Turner requiring consideration of all circumstantial evidence and nexus to discrimination.

propositions.text: Board did not explicitly state considering all allegations as whole but Decision shows it recognized obligation to do so
Court not prepared to conclude Board failed to do what it recognized it was obliged to do

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Board recognized its obligation to consider all allegations as a whole and did not fail to do so.

propositions.text: Evidence of discrimination was not compelling enough to render Board's failure to discuss whole evidence unreasonable
Court cannot reach own conclusions on evidence to find Board unreasonable

paragraphs.summary: The court finds discrimination evidence not compelling and cannot substitute its own conclusions for the Board's.

propositions.text: Court concludes Board's analysis of discrimination grievance was reasonable

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes the Board's analysis of the discrimination grievance was reasonable.

propositions.text: Court grants judicial review application in part, sets aside paragraph 495 on salary and benefits, remits to Board
Court dismisses application in all other respects

paragraphs.summary: The court grants judicial review in part, sets aside salary award paragraph, remits to Board, and dismisses other claims.

propositions.text: Court awards Ms. Sahadeo costs of $2500 due to substantial financial success

paragraphs.summary: The court awards Ms. Sahadeo costs of $2500 due to partial financial success.

propositions.text: Respondent requests style of cause be amended to identify Attorney General as sole respondent
Ms. Sahadeo does not object to style of cause amendment
Court grants request and amends style of cause accordingly

paragraphs.summary: The respondent requests and Ms. Sahadeo agrees to amend style of cause; court grants and amends accordingly.
